---
title: "Bundle format"
subtitle: "The portable JSON record shared by the R, Python, and Julia implementations: schema 1.1."
---



A `taxodist` bundle is a single JSON file that stores a complete analysis: how every input name was resolved, the lineages (and their ranks) that were used, the distance matrix, the metric definition, and where the data came from. Bundles are written by `write_taxodist_bundle()`, read by `read_taxodist_bundle()`, and compared with `compare_bundles()` in all three languages. A bundle written in one language is read by the other two without differences.

- **JSON Schema:** [`taxodist-bundle-v1.schema.json`](schema/taxodist-bundle-v1.schema.json) (JSON Schema draft 2020-12; also shipped inside the R package under `schema/` and in the Python package).
- **Example bundle:** [`example.taxodist.json`](examples/example.taxodist.json), produced offline by the R code below.

## Versioning policy

| Schema | Written by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `1.0` | taxodist 0.8.0 and 0.9.0 | Reciprocal metric only; no ranks |
| `1.1` | taxodist 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 | Adds the metric choice (and, for `"ranked"`, its rank levels) and `lineage_ranks` |

- Versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 write schema **1.1**; version 1.1.0 did not change the format.
- Every 1.x release reads schema **1.0 and 1.1**. A schema 1.0 bundle must use the reciprocal metric (`inverse_mrca_depth`).
- The bundle format and the metric definitions are stable for the 1.x series: later 1.x releases continue to read bundles written by 1.0.0. A file whose `schema_version` is not `1.0` or `1.1` is rejected.

## Top-level fields

All top-level fields are required, and no other fields are allowed.

| Field | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | string | Always `"taxodist_bundle"` |
| `schema_version` | string | `"1.1"` (or `"1.0"` for older files) |
| `created_at` | string or null | Creation time, e.g. `"2026-11-24 12:03:08 UTC"` |
| `source` | object | Provenance of the lineages (below) |
| `software` | object | Implementation that wrote the bundle (below) |
| `metric` | object | Distance definition used for `matrix` (below) |
| `taxa` | array | One record per input label, in input order (below) |
| `matrix` | object | Labeled square distance matrix (below) |

### `source`

| Field | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `"The Taxonomicon"` for live retrievals from the default source; since 1.1.0, the name of the Open Tree Taxonomy (including its version) or `"NCBI Taxonomy"` for resolutions made with `source = "ott"` or `"ncbi"` (see [Taxonomic sources](sources.qmd)); or the `source` given to `taxo_from_lineages()` (default `"user-supplied"`) |
| `url` | string or null | Source URL, `null` for user-supplied lineages |
| `retrieved_at` | string or null | Retrieval time |

### `software`

| Field | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Always `"taxodist"` |
| `version` | string or null | Package version, e.g. `"1.0.0"` |
| `language` | string | `"R"`, `"Python"`, or `"Julia"` |

### `metric`

| Field | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `"inverse_mrca_depth"` (`metric = "reciprocal"`), `"path_length"` (`"path"`), `"wu_palmer"`, or `"ranked_path_length"` (`"ranked"`) |
| `definition` | string | Human-readable definition |
| `root_depth` | number | Always `1` |
| `common_ancestor` | string | Always `"continuous common lineage prefix"` |
| `rank_levels` | array of strings | Required for `ranked_path_length` only: the rank levels used, by default `kingdom`, `phylum`, `class`, `order`, `family`, `genus`, `species` |

### `taxa`

Each element describes one input label.

| Field | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | string | Input label as supplied |
| `resolved_name` | string or null | Name of the selected entry |
| `id` | string or null | Taxonomicon ID, or `custom:<label>` for user-supplied lineages without identifiers |
| `status` | string | `"resolved"`, `"ambiguous"`, `"unresolved"`, or `"retrieval_error"` |
| `n_candidates` | integer | Number of candidate entries found |
| `lineage_depth` | integer or null | Number of lineage nodes, root included |
| `lineage` | array of strings or null | Root-to-tip lineage |
| `candidates` | array | Every candidate as `{"id": ..., "name": ...}` |
| `lineage_ranks` | array or null | Schema 1.1, optional: rank of each lineage node, aligned with `lineage`; `null` for unranked nodes |

The schema enforces consistency with `status`: resolved and ambiguous records have a name, an identifier, a non-empty lineage, and at least one candidate; unresolved records have no name, identifier, lineage, or candidates; retrieval errors have no name, identifier, or lineage.

### `matrix`

| Field | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `labels` | array of strings | Row and column labels, in input order |
| `values` | array of arrays | Square, symmetric matrix of distances |

Each value is a number, `null` for a missing distance (a taxon that could not be resolved), or the string `"Infinity"` (`"-Infinity"`) for lineages without a common root.

## Validation

Beyond the JSON Schema, readers and writers check that candidate counts match the candidates, that `lineage_depth` matches the lineage, that the matrix labels match the `taxa` records, that the matrix is symmetric, and that every stored distance agrees with the stored lineages under the stored metric. Using a bundle in memory (printing it or passing it to `distance_matrix()`) checks its structure only.

## Example

The example bundle was produced offline from three curated lineages:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
res <- taxo_from_lineages(
  list(
    Tyrannosaurus = c("Biota", "Animalia", "Chordata", "Dinosauria", "Theropoda", "Tyrannosaurus"),
    Velociraptor  = c("Biota", "Animalia", "Chordata", "Dinosauria", "Theropoda", "Velociraptor"),
    Homo          = c("Biota", "Animalia", "Chordata", "Mammalia", "Primates", "Homo")
  ),
  ranks = list(
    Tyrannosaurus = c(NA, "Kingdom", "Phylum", NA, NA, "Genus"),
    Velociraptor  = c(NA, "Kingdom", "Phylum", NA, NA, "Genus"),
    Homo          = c(NA, "Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Genus")
  )
)
bundle <- taxo_bundle(res)
bundle
#> 
#> ── taxodist Bundle ──
#> 
#> • Schema: 1.1
#> • Created: 2026-11-25 11:43:26 UTC
#> • Taxa: 3
#> • Resolved: 3
#> • Ambiguous: 0
#> • Unresolved: 0
#> • Retrieval errors: 0

file <- tempfile(fileext = ".taxodist.json")
write_taxodist_bundle(bundle, file)
distance_matrix(read_taxodist_bundle(file))
#>              Tyrannosaurus Velociraptor
#> Velociraptor     0.2000000             
#> Homo             0.3333333    0.3333333
```
:::


The file written by `write_taxodist_bundle()` ([download](examples/example.taxodist.json)):

```json
{
  "format": "taxodist_bundle",
  "schema_version": "1.1",
  "created_at": "2026-11-24 12:03:08 UTC",
  "source": {
    "name": "user-supplied",
    "url": null,
    "retrieved_at": "2026-11-24 12:03:08 UTC"
  },
  "software": {
    "name": "taxodist",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "language": "R"
  },
  "metric": {
    "name": "inverse_mrca_depth",
    "definition": "0 for identical lineages; otherwise 1 / depth(MRCA)",
    "root_depth": 1,
    "common_ancestor": "continuous common lineage prefix"
  },
  "taxa": [
    {
      "input": "Tyrannosaurus",
      "resolved_name": "Tyrannosaurus",
      "id": "custom:Tyrannosaurus",
      "status": "resolved",
      "n_candidates": 1,
      "lineage_depth": 6,
      "lineage": ["Biota", "Animalia", "Chordata", "Dinosauria", "Theropoda", "Tyrannosaurus"],
      "candidates": [
        { "id": "custom:Tyrannosaurus", "name": "Tyrannosaurus" }
      ],
      "lineage_ranks": [null, "Kingdom", "Phylum", null, null, "Genus"]
    },
    {
      "input": "Velociraptor",
      "...": "same structure as above"
    },
    {
      "input": "Homo",
      "...": "same structure as above"
    }
  ],
  "matrix": {
    "labels": ["Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor", "Homo"],
    "values": [
      [0, 0.2, 0.333333333333333],
      [0.2, 0, 0.333333333333333],
      [0.333333333333333, 0.333333333333333, 0]
    ]
  }
}
```

The listing above abbreviates two `taxa` records and compacts arrays for readability; the downloadable file is complete and valid against the schema.

The same file can be read in the other languages:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```r
bundle <- read_taxodist_bundle("example.taxodist.json")
distance_matrix(bundle)
```

### Python

```python
import taxodist as td

bundle = td.read_taxodist_bundle("example.taxodist.json")
td.distance_matrix(bundle)
```

### Julia

```julia
using Taxodist

bundle = read_taxodist_bundle("example.taxodist.json")
distance_matrix(bundle)
```

:::
